text: An arcade for good rivals, close matches and verifiable results. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate.

section: Pong is back. Bring a rival.
text: PONGIT is a head-to-head Pong arcade on Monad Testnet. Move your paddle, bring a rival and race to seven points. The browser draws the action; Solidity contracts determine collisions, scores, winners and ratings. All balances, bets and prizes use test MON, chain 10143. Ordinary ranked wins award ELO, not MON. Gameplay gas is sponsored while the platform has funding.

Matchmaking finds a ranked opponent in your selected Classic or Chaos mode. Invite someone sends a friendly duel to a contact, username or wallet address. Create room opens a shared cabinet for up to eight people, with a shareable link and winner-stays rotation. Choose Classic or Chaos above the cards. Both players accept the same duel before it starts. Connect once with a Mera passkey and reuse the scoped game session. Rooms guide.

The account button lets you save a unique username and choose from twelve character portraits. Ranking is directly in the header, with separate Classic and Chaos ELO. Friendly rooms and invitations leave rankings unchanged. The account's Betting credit & wallet panel separates wallet funds, rooms credit and recent market positions.

Chaos spectators can back a player between rallies. Stronger betting support can shrink that player's paddle for the next exchange. These testnet bets execute on Monad; a provisional VPS attester brings paid totals to the hosted game. Chaos rules and limits. New testnet room markets pay automatically after the first Interlude result is published on Monad. This early payment can precede protocol finality; later disputes are logged. Previous markets keep their original settlement rules. Payments. V4 arcade keeps the previous tournaments, markets, payments, notebook, replays and balances available separately. Old vaults do not transfer automatically. The technical guides distinguish each deployment rather than treating all historical functionality as one contract.
From Play now to your first seven points.

On your first visit, choose Enter arcade for audio or Enter muted. The choice is remembered; you can change it in Arcade settings. Classic is the initial mode, with Ranked · Free to play shown under the main button. Select Play now. Create a passkey, or continue with the account you already use. Approve the limited arcade session when requested. PONGIT continues into matchmaking automatically. Wait for an opponent and the onchain match to start. You do not need a public profile before playing. Cancelling the connection abandons that Play now request. If you already have an active match, use Resume match.

Use W / S or ↑ / ↓. On a touch screen, hold the up/down controls beneath the court. Release to stop. The match header shows whether you control the left or right paddle. The first player to score seven points wins. The solid paddle previews your movement immediately; a score or collision becomes authoritative when confirmed by the contract. Understand the confirmation delay.

Cabinet tools contains session actions and Concede. Opening an overlay or losing focus clears held controls. Conceding ends your participation with a loss; it is different from cancelling a queue search before a match exists. If your session expires, use Reconnect to renew it. Do not create a new passkey to recover an existing player.

The confirmed result triggers a skippable four-second VICTORY or DEFEAT sequence. Then choose Rematch, Watch replay or Find another opponent. Rematch invites the player you just faced; they must accept. Ranked games update the appropriate ELO ladder. Ordinary victories do not pay MON.
Keep your account, renew your session and understand what you sign.

PONGIT uses Mera and a passkey provider that supports WebAuthn PRF. Use the HTTPS site at pongit.xyz. No wallet extension is required. Create a passkey creates an account using a new credential. Continue as… uses the remembered account and credential. Use another passkey opens the provider's account selection. Forget this account removes the browser's remembered hint. It does not delete the passkey or onchain funds. An unsupported provider produces a compatibility error. Use a PRF-compatible provider rather than repeatedly creating credentials. Recovering the same account requires the same passkey and working provider support; a username is not an account recovery method.

After connection, approve a limited gameplay authorization lasting up to two hours. It allows matchmaking, accepting challenges, match consent, paddle control and conceding your own match. The limited key and authorization are kept in sessionStorage, so F5 in the same tab can recover the session. The browser remembers the wallet address, credential identifier and domain separately. Wallet keys and decrypted notebook contents are not saved in those stores. Only one tab may control a game for a given account and deployment. Keep the controlling tab open. Closing it ends its local session storage.

When the session expires, the header displays Reconnect. Clicking it renews the session directly. Play now also carries your intention through renewal into matchmaking. No passkey popup should appear automatically while you play. Spending still needs a separate owner passkey approval: bets, withdrawals, tournament registration and administration are not covered by the arcade grant.

Open the account button and select Disconnect. PONGIT closes the notebook, clears local session material and requests onchain revocation. If the network is unavailable, the interface explicitly reports that revocation is not yet confirmed. Clearing the browser alone does not revoke an authorization already onchain; its expiry still applies. Physical cross-device passkey recovery depends on your provider. Automated browser tests do not establish that every physical device/provider combination works. Permission details.
Two paddles. One ball. First to seven.

Classic is PONGIT's standard Pong mode. The logical court is 1024 × 576 units. Both paddles have a height of 96 units. The ball and paddle speeds follow the fixed match rules; the first player to seven points wins. Move vertically with W/S, the arrow keys or the touch controls. Walls reflect the ball. A paddle impact is resolved against its confirmed position. Missing the ball gives the opponent a point.

Play now joins Classic ranked matchmaking by default. A direct challenge defaults to friendly, with ranked available under Match options. Both players consent to the opponent, mode and ranking choice before match creation. Ranked results change the Classic ELO only. Friendly results do not change either ladder. See rankings and seasons.

Spectators may place eligible test-MON bets when the market is open. In Classic, betting pressure does not change paddle sizes. That mechanic belongs to Chaos. Participants cannot bet on their own match using their participant account.

The browser previews motion but contracts decide impacts, points and results. A local visual correction is not a new rule or a second paddle. Open Network details if input delay affects play. The match does not become a private offline game when your connection drops. Reconnect to recover its current state. Concede ends the match as a loss; a technical cancellation is a different confirmed result with different market accounting. Classic is also the mode used in the current single-elimination tournaments. An ordinary Classic win awards ELO when ranked, with no automatic MON victory bonus.
Try the dedicated Classic friendly arena and distinguish live results from Monad commitments.

Open More, then Interlude lab, or visit the lab directly. It opens separately from the main arcade. One shared arena supports Classic friendly matches and public spectators. Rules 3 remain first to seven, with ordinary paddle heights and speed. The ball is 50% faster than the main arcade: 192 horizontal and 96 vertical logical units per second. Each successful paddle return adds 10% to both velocity components, with no gameplay speed cap. Wall bounces do not accelerate the ball. Every point resets the next serve to its starting speed. The court displays the current rally-speed multiplier. Existing main-arcade rules are unchanged. The main arcade still provides ranked matchmaking, Chaos, tournaments, betting, payouts and indexed replays. Lab matches do not award ELO or MON and are not added to those rankings, markets or replay archives. The lab cannot access an existing betting vault.

Choose Connect passkey, or Continue as for a remembered account. Use the same Mera passkey as the main arcade to retain your wallet address. A separate signature opens a 30-minute Interlude grant limited to the lab's game methods. The generated game key and signed grant stay in this tab's session storage. Wallet keys are closed after signing and are not stored there. The faster-ball deployment uses a new contract, so an old lab grant cannot authorize it. Connect explicitly once to approve the new scoped session. F5 restores an unexpired grant without a new passkey ceremony. Only one tab may control the lab with a given account. Reconnect lab session reloads the grant and current state after an uncertain command. If the grant expired or was revoked, the connection dialog lets you authorize another grant. A recovery never silently resends an invitation or concession. Disconnect lab removes this tab's game key. It does not revoke every Interlude grant onchain: a copy of the grant remains valid until its expiry. It also does not disconnect the main arcade. Interlude's account-wide revocation changes the Hub epoch on Monad and requires a separate wallet transaction; the lab does not provide a sponsored revocation control.

Enter an optional rival wallet address and choose Create friendly match. An empty address creates an open invitation. Choose Copy invitation and share the link. The recipient connects and chooses Accept & play. A targeted invitation only accepts its intended account; an open invitation reserves the first other account accepted by the contract. Invitations expire after ten minutes. Cancel invitation closes an unaccepted invitation. An old link never accepts a newer match automatically. If the arena is already occupied, watch it until the current game ends. Use W / S, the arrow keys or the on-screen movement buttons. A release or direction change replaces an unsent intention. Submitted commands remain serialized with sequential nonces. Opening a dialog or losing focus requests a stop; a network outage can prevent that request reaching the engine. Concede ends your current match. At seven points, participants automatically see VICTORY or DEFEAT, with a skippable four-second animation. Spectators see a neutral winner announcement. Rematch invites the same rival, who chooses Accept & play. Create open invitation starts an invitation for another opponent. Reloading a completed match does not replay the celebration; View result reopens it without animation.

The court displays the engine's current state with bounded local rendering. The lower panel independently reads the latest Monad snapshot. At the end, it compares the same match's terminal result hash on the engine and on Monad. An engine receipt is not a Monad transaction receipt. A matching committed hash means Monad contains that result, but Interlude's optimistic challenge window has not necessarily closed. No financial settlement uses a lab result. The initial dedicated-node probe on 7 September 2026 completed 200 direction changes with a median SDK call time of 29 ms, p95 of 35 ms and p99 of 44 ms from the test connection. It observed the final result hash on Monad about 2.1 seconds after the live result observation. These are samples from that run, not service guarantees or measurements from every player's location.

If a command cannot be confirmed, the lab stops submitting and displays a recovery message. Wait for Engine online, inspect the current arena and choose Reconnect lab session. Expiry, revocation or a changed node clock can require operator intervention. No background request prompts a passkey during play. The lab contract is 0xbe51fea690699ad07e4eb5932c4d131689072999 on Monad Testnet. Interlude operates the engine and owns the shipped contract. The base chain ID is 10143; this dedicated engine exposes chain ID 4242 and a measured 10 ms virtual block cadence. The deployment is immutable and isolated from V4 funds. See the reviewed implementation and deployment record and Interlude's live/settled model.

Classic and Chaos, private contacts and rotating shared cabinets. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate. The homepage opens the Interlude multi-room arcade. Access depends on an active operator delegation; new admissions pause when it expires or cannot be verified. Scheduled renewal drains current games and includes an onchain challenge period before new games resume. The V4 arcade remains available separately.

Matchmaking finds a ranked opponent in the selected Classic or Chaos mode. The queues are separate. Invite someone opens contacts and username or wallet-address search for a friendly duel. Create room opens a shared cabinet with up to eight people, including the two current players. Connect once with your existing Mera passkey. The chosen action continues after connection or renewal. An unexpired Interlude session is restored after F5 in the same tab. Each deployment has its own game authorization. Your wallet address stays the same. A rooms grant lasts 30 minutes and can accept a match, move a paddle, advance its physics, cancel a pending match or concede. It cannot spend betting credit, withdraw MON or administer the contracts. The wallet key is closed after authorization. Disconnect removes this tab's game key; it does not revoke copies on other devices.

A targeted invitation is reserved for its recipient and expires after ten minutes. A group-room link requests one of the available seats. The invitation shows the identity and Accept / Back. Accepting a room invitation also accepts its first proposed duel when available. Every pairing requires both players' approval of the same signed ticket within twenty seconds. Back, or failing to respond, marks a player away. Rejoin queue places them at the end of the room queue. A submitted acceptance is checked on the engine before cancellation. The coordinator cannot invent a score or choose a winner.

Two members play while the others automatically see the match. After a verified result, the winner stays and the loser moves to the end of the queue. The next available member is proposed. With two members, both can accept another game. Leaving the room transfers the host role to the longest-present member. A connection loss is not a concession. During a match, Members opens the room list and Tools contains network status and Concede. Copy address and Copy room link provide a brief confirmation or a manual copy field when the clipboard is unavailable. The court remains rectangular, with the score and touch controls visible. Technical panels and financial forms do not sit below it. A player can occupy one room or matchmaking queue at a time. Empty rooms expire after thirty minutes; inactive rooms expire after twenty-four hours. Initially, two matches can run concurrently. Other rooms remain open and display Waiting for an arena while publication capacity is unavailable.

Save or remove a contact by username or address. This is a private, server-stored address book without friendship requests. It is separate from the encrypted Mera notebook. Suggested rivals are the eight most frequent opponents in the last thirty days, using verified Interlude and V1 to V4 results, with the most recent encounter breaking ties. Existing invitation blocks also apply in rooms.

Games remain first to seven. Each successful paddle return increases ball velocity by ten percent, without a gameplay speed cap; every point resets the next serve. Walls do not increase speed. Classic carries forward the previous rooms ELO. Chaos starts a separate rating at 1000. The header has one Ranking entry with a mode selector. The contract applies placements, diminishing gains for repeated pairings and one rating update per result. Rooms and direct invitations are friendly and leave ELO unchanged. Live ELO and its published Monad copy are shown separately. Publication remains subject to Interlude's challenge process. Chaos rooms offer between-rally prediction markets to spectators through Market. They use a separate vault, and payouts wait for delegation finality. Ordinary wins never award a MON prize. V4 arcade retains its original Chaos, tournaments, markets, payouts, notebook, rankings and replays. Existing vaults are not migrated, and old match links continue to refer to their original contracts. Rooms retain result summaries, not an unlimited recording of gameplay frames.

The rooms account opens Betting credit & wallet for credits, signed withdrawals and recent positions. In Chaos, the testnet VPS bridge attests the MON actually paid at a fixed cutoff. Each window is 40 Monad blocks, approximately twelve seconds, plus publication and confirmation delays. The game waits at that boundary. Chaos rules. New games pause during scheduled delegation renewal. New testnet markets pay to the fixed wallet after the first published Interlude result, even if the recipient is disconnected. Later disputes are logged. Previous markets still wait for the delegation's challenge period. Payment states.

Understand how betting pressure changes the next rally. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate.

Chaos keeps the first-to-seven objective, but accepted betting costs influence paddle height. The player receiving more support can become harder to defend. Select Chaos above the three home cards before matchmaking, inviting a rival or creating a room. Room members inherit its mode. The V4 arcade retains its own Chaos controls. The calculation uses the MON actually paid for accepted bets on each side. Seed liquidity supplied by the platform is excluded, and later payouts do not erase the accumulated pressure. Condition Paddle height Total accepted costs below 0.002 MON Both remain at 96 units A player's share is at most 60% That player remains at 96 Share is 80% Approximately 84 units Share reaches 100% Minimum 72 units Above 60%, the reduction increases linearly up to 25%. Integer rounding is applied by the contract. Paddle speed does not change.

After a nonfinal point, a Chaos room pauses. Once the exact pause is published on Monad, its market opens for 40 blocks, approximately twelve seconds. The VPS freezes actual paid totals at the cutoff after two further confirmations and signs a checkpoint scoped to that match and rally. This is a provisional testnet trust assumption. The engine applies the resulting heights and freezes them for the next rally. Publication, passkey submission and confirmation can extend the pause beyond twelve seconds. A missing checkpoint keeps play paused; it never silently substitutes zero pressure. Concede remains available. The original V4 arena still uses its three-second match-clock intermission and two-block closing guard. An already resolved collision is never recalculated with a new size. If the chain needs to catch up, simulation stops at the intermission before entering the next rally with its new parameters. More support can shrink the player you are backing. Review the Chaos warning and the cost before approving a bet. Concentration of shares is not the same as concentration of MON paid.

The room shows the intermission countdown, then Waiting for the betting checkpoint when more time is needed. The two visible paddles use their individual confirmed heights. Without enough accepted bets, Chaos can look like Classic. Chaos has its own ranked queue and ELO. Friendly Chaos challenges change no ranking. Current tournaments remain Classic. Betting guide.
Find an opponent or invite the rival you already know.

Select Classic or Chaos and press Play now. Ranked matchmaking uses separate queues for the two modes. While searching, the waiting screen shows the mode, elapsed time and cancellation state. Cancel search cancels an unsubmitted search with signed authorization. Once a match creation transaction is submitted, the interface shows the real transaction state; it cannot pretend to undo that transaction.

Open Rivals, or use Challenge a friend from home. Search for a public username or a full wallet address, and select the profile. You can also paste an address into Opponent address. Expand Match options to choose Classic/Chaos and friendly/ranked. Friendly is the initial choice outside rematches. Select Send challenge. The recipient receives an Accept / Decline notification, including when they are on another screen. Accepting continues through consent and match creation automatically. Challenge is also available beside leaderboard entries.

Rematch sends a 60-second invitation to the previous opponent with the same mode and friendly/ranked choice. After a tournament, the rematch is independent of the bracket and charges no tournament entry fee. Other challenges last ten minutes. Shareable links is a secondary option: an addressed link stays reserved for its recipient; an open link reserves the first accepted opponent atomically. Share the generated URL, not a screenshot of your passkey.

Only one match creation can be active per player. Crossed rematch requests and repeated clicks are deduplicated. A busy opponent must finish their current activity before another game can start. You can decline, cancel an unsubmitted invitation, or block unwanted invitations. Blocked players can be unblocked in Rivals. Rate limits prevent invitation spam. After a network interruption, the inbox refreshes; consult its actual status before sending another invitation.

Separate Classic and Chaos ladders, with results recorded onchain. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate.

Open Ranking directly in the header and choose Classic or Chaos. The previous V4 ladders are available separately. Each mode has a separate onchain ELO. New players start at 1000. Classic inherits the previous rooms rating. The new rooms Chaos ladder starts at 1000; the V4 Chaos ranking remains separate. Saved usernames and avatars appear beside rankings. The wallet address remains the verifiable identity behind each profile.

Ranked wins and losses use an expected score calculated from the two ratings. Beating a stronger opponent generally gains more than beating a weaker opponent. Friendly matches change neither rating. The first ten recorded games in that rating's placement count use a K factor of 64; later results use 32. Integer rounding applies and the rating has a floor of 100. Do not expect the two players' displayed changes always to be identical: placement factors can differ. Repeated ranked meetings with the same opponent in the same mode and UTC day have decreasing impact. The change is divided by that pair's daily meeting count, capped at a divisor of eight.

Seasons last 30 days from the current game's genesis time. Ratings owned by the current deployment move halfway toward 1000 for each elapsed season, evaluated lazily when read. The contract caps catch-up at 16 steps per read calculation. Ratings not yet materialized in the current deployment are read from the previous game, so inheritance follows that previous contract's own season rules.

section: If a ranking is not updated yet
text: The rooms contract applies a ranked result once on the engine. The leaderboard distinguishes live ELO from the published Monad copy, which remains subject to the delegation challenge process. The coordinator verifies and caches these views; V4 rankings continue through Envio. Wait for confirmation and refresh if the display is temporarily behind; changing your username does not reset your ELO. Use Challenge beside a player to invite them. Challenge options.
Join a Classic bracket and play each round from the tournament screen.

Open More → Tournaments. Each card shows its capacity, registered players, entry cost, prize and current state. Current tournaments are Classic ranked, with single-elimination brackets of 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32 players. Select Register and approve the registration with your owner passkey. If an entry fee exists, it is debited from betting credit. Registration is an owner-authorized operation even for a free entry. A registered account cannot enter the same tournament twice.

Start bracket is available only when the contract's conditions are satisfied. A tournament must fill its advertised capacity; it can start when full, or after its closing time if still full. A partially filled bracket does not silently resize. Entrants are seeded by Classic ELO, with deterministic address ordering for equal ratings. In an active round, press Play round. Both opponents join that tournament pairing; generic matchmaking is not a substitute for the round button. The relayer attaches eligible matches and advances completed rounds automatically. Wait for the confirmed result and updated bracket before the next round. A cancelled match can be replaced under the tournament's contract rules.

The winner receives the seeded prize plus accepted entry fees directly in their wallet through V4's payout accounting. They do not need to remain connected or sign to receive it. Cancellation is permitted after registration closes without a full bracket, or after an active round exceeds 12,000 blocks. The confirmed cancellation enables automatic entry-fee refunds. The seeded contribution returns to the fixed treasury separately. A rejected wallet transfer becomes a reserved, retryable payment. Payment states.
Rematch creates an independent challenge against the same opponent, with no new entry fee. It does not replay or modify a tournament bracket result.
Follow the arena as a spectator without a wallet connection.

Use Watch live on the home cabinet or Live in the navigation. Select a current match to follow its score and court. You do not need a passkey just to watch. The match header labels the view as SPECTATOR VIEW. It shows the mode and whether the match is ranked or friendly. If a player has a public username, that name replaces the shortened address in the scoreboard.

Spectators receive network snapshots and see a rendered preview between confirmations. The contracts still determine impacts and points. LIVE PREVIEW, AWAITING IMPACT CONFIRMATION or SYNCING / PREVIEW PAUSED describe the display's relationship to confirmed state. In Chaos, the rally banner shows each paddle's size and whether the match is in intermission. A betting-induced handicap changes the next rally, not the current collision. At a confirmed result, spectators see a neutral winner announcement rather than a personal VICTORY or DEFEAT celebration.

Eligible spectators can connect a passkey and use the match's market. Review the cost and potential payout before approving any test-MON spend. A participant's account cannot bet on its own game. Learn about betting.

An empty Live list means there are no listed active matches. If the feed disconnects, wait for reconnection and a fresh snapshot. The visual pause does not establish that the onchain game paused. After completion, the result remains available; a replay is available only while it satisfies the retention policy.
Revisit your last three finished games and understand replay availability.

Open More → Replays. The personal list shows up to three played and finished matches, across Classic, Chaos and all four deployments. A cancellation before play starts does not consume a slot. Each replay is stored once. It remains retained while it belongs to either participant's most recent three eligible games. As a result, an older match may still be retained for your opponent even after it leaves your personal list.

Choose an available replay, or use Watch replay after a result. Play replay / Pause replay controls playback; the timeline moves between recorded states. The replay is reconstructed from confirmed state, with the rules and Chaos handicap data belonging to that deployment. Note this moment pauses playback and opens the private notebook context for that versioned match and timestamp. Unlock your notebook, add your observation and use Save encrypted to persist it.

Available: recorded frames can be loaded. Indexing: the necessary indexed data has not arrived yet; retry after the indexer catches up. Retired: replay frames were removed by retention. Refreshing will not recreate them automatically. A retired replay still has its result summary, score and financial rights. Your encrypted notes are preserved and indicate that the replay is retired. The blockchain still contains the original events; the application does not provide an unlimited replay reindexing service.
Match references include the deployment, such as v4:12 or v2:12. Those are different matches. Historical results and older vault rights remain separate. Legacy balances.
Choose a unique name and your character in the arcade.

section: Put your name on the cabinet
text: From home, select Create your profile beneath the cabinet, or Edit your profile if you already have one. Connecting or renewing continues into the editor without starting matchmaking. The same editor is under Rivals → Your public profile. Your profile is optional. Playing without one displays your shortened wallet address.

Use 3–20 characters, starting with a letter. Letters, digits and underscores are accepted; names are normalized to lowercase. Neon_Rider and neon_rider are therefore the same name. The availability message is a preview, not a reservation. Save public profile performs the authoritative uniqueness check. If someone saves that name first, choose a different one. Saving requires authentication as the connected account.

The roster contains Nova, Ghost, Vector, Pulse, Drift, Kitsune, Ion, Echo, Onyx, Glitch, Solar and Viper. Select a portrait to update the large preview, then save. Character names are shared presets; your username is what must be unique. You can use arrow keys within the roster, Home/End for its first/last character, and Tab to leave. The selected border and checkmark identify your choice. There is no image-upload feature in this release.

Your saved username and avatar follow you into home, Rivals and the leaderboard. The scoreboard displays the username, while the linked wallet address remains verifiable. F5 reloads the saved profile from the server. Remove my public profile removes the public tag, not your passkey, results, ELO or funds. Public names and avatars are separate from private notebook nicknames and notes. Unsaved changes are not a new published profile.
Keep favourite rivals, private nicknames and timestamped replay notes.

Open Rivals and find Your private playbook. Unlock notebook uses the same passkey as your account but a separate Mera PRF namespace and encryption key. Public profile names and avatars are not stored in this notebook. The decrypted content and key stay in memory. The server stores only ciphertext and technical metadata such as a revision and encryption IV.

Add a favourite rival's full address and a private nickname. These names do not reserve public usernames or change another player's profile. Open a match or replay, then use Note this moment to attach an observation to its versioned reference and timestamp. Choose a preferred mode and sound preference. Apply preferences updates this browser; finish an active match or queue search first. Remove individual rivals or notes with their delete controls.

Edits remain in memory until you select Save encrypted. Each save uses fresh encryption randomness. Lock, disconnecting or changing account closes the decrypted notebook. Reload saved copy (discard local edits) replaces your unsaved changes with the server's version. If another device saved first, PONGIT reports a revision conflict; preserve any edits you need before choosing to reload and merge manually. Recovering on another device requires the same PRF-capable passkey. A new passkey derives a different key and cannot decrypt the old notebook. Physical cross-device compatibility has not been established for every provider.

Your notes remain even when a replay is retired; the note indicates that its replay is no longer retained. Public blockchain activity remains public. Encryption of stored notes does not protect decrypted content from a compromised browser or an extension capable of reading the page's live memory.

Know where your test MON is held and how to withdraw it. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate.

In the rooms account, open Betting credit & wallet. Wallet balance is native MON at your Mera address. Betting credit is held in the rooms vault. Get test betting credit requests a one-time 0.02 MON credit per account in this deployment, with a master-passkey signature and service funding limits. Withdraw credit to wallet signs a withdrawal of currently available rooms credit to your own address. The game session cannot authorize it. Your recent positions opens a match's payment state and receipt. Receiving winnings needs no signature, but the result must first pass delegation finality. Previous balances opens the separate V4 arcade; it does not merge or move funds. The rest of this article describes the preserved V4 balance controls.

Open the account button in the header. The account panel shows the full address, an explorer link and separate balances. Balance Purpose Wallet Native test MON held by your Mera account; V4 winnings arrive here Betting balance Available credit held in the active vault for authorized bets and tournament entry fees Legacy vaults Separate balances belonging to V1, V2 and V3 Receiving a prize in your wallet does not automatically put it back into betting credit. There is no automatic reinvestment.

Use Get test credits from the account panel. The application verifies an owner-signed request and applies its funding and abuse limits. Credits are for this testnet application, not mainnet currency. The daily sponsorship ceiling is disabled, but relayer funding, transaction limits and rate limits still apply. If funding is unavailable, the interface reports it. Repeated clicking cannot create funds; wait for the service to recover.

Expand Withdraw test MON, enter the recipient and an amount within the available betting balance, then select Sign withdrawal and approve with your owner passkey. The arcade session cannot authorize a withdrawal. Wait for the actual transaction confirmation before treating the wallet balance as updated.

Expand Older balances to access V1–V3 separately. Their eligible claims or refunds credit that version's vault, followed by a signed withdrawal to your wallet. They do not gain V4's direct-wallet behaviour retroactively. Always check the selected version and its balance. No migration automatically moves old funds or combines four vaults into one. A retired replay does not remove the claim or withdrawal right. For new V4 positions, automatic payouts replace the old claim workflow. An ordinary match does not create a MON prize for its winner.
Tune the music, test the effects and make the cabinet comfortable.

PONGIT plays Last Stop in full and loops it. Music by Karl Casey @ White Bat Audio. The credit also appears in the application and follows the artist's usage conditions. Choose Enter arcade or Enter muted on your first visit. In Arcade settings, music defaults to 20% and effects to 60%; saved values take precedence. The music continues between game screens, ducks during play and jingles, and pauses in a hidden tab.

Use Test sound to activate or resume the browser's audio context. Settings distinguish enabled, muted, suspended, loading and failed states. The browser may require a click or key press before allowing sound. If the test reports a generated signal but you hear nothing, check the tab's mute state, system volume, output device and headphones. A signal measurement cannot verify the physical speaker you are using. Check effects volume separately from music volume. Button actions, invitations, matching, countdowns, rebounds, points, handicap changes and outcomes have distinct effects. Points and results follow confirmation; reconnecting should not replay a backlog of sounds.

Under Room appearance, toggle Background effects or choose Subtle / Full arcade. The room remains a static illustration. With effects enabled, small 16-bit decorations on the cabinet play short, staggered animations with quiet pauses between loops, including during matches. They never enter the court or make sounds. Turning effects off leaves those decorations still. They also stop when outside the viewport or when the tab is hidden. Your device's reduced-motion preference displays a fixed frame. Documentation ornaments always stay still. PONGIT follows your device's reduced-motion preference. Result sequences can be skipped immediately; after skipping, the result actions remain accessible. Their foreground can scroll while the page behind is locked.

Paddle shortcuts work only in a controllable match. Dialogs contain keyboard focus, close with Escape when their action allows it, and return focus afterward. Opening an overlay or losing focus releases held controls. The touch arrows support holding and releasing, including pointer cancellation. Documentation has its own quiet reading view and does not start the arcade's audio.

Review the cost, signed maximum and potential payout before supporting a player. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate.

Join a Chaos room as a spectator and open Market in the top bar. Connect your passkey to use the market. Classic rooms do not open betting markets; the V4 arcade retains its own markets. Choose which player to back and the number of shares. Purchases use the active betting balance, not an automatic debit from incoming wallet winnings. A winning share pays 1 MON per whole share; fractional shares pay proportionally. The displayed potential payout is the gross payment if that side wins, not profit in addition to your purchase cost. Losing shares pay zero.

The review shows the selected player, Estimated cost, Signed maximum and Payout if this player wins. In rooms, the maximum adds a 3% tolerance and conservative rounding to the displayed quote. The V4 review retains its 1% tolerance. The signed maximum bounds the spend. Quotes are state-dependent and can become stale while your passkey prompt is open. Select Confirm bet with passkey only after reviewing the current details. If the market state changes beyond the permitted amount or closes, refresh the quote and review again. A gameplay key has no permission to approve a bet. The account panel offers Get test betting credit and Withdraw credit to wallet, both with owner approval. Wallet winnings are not automatically deposited as betting credit.

PONGIT uses a binary LMSR market maker. Buying shares changes the cost of subsequent purchases according to the outstanding shares and configured liquidity. The platform deposits real test-MON liquidity; the contract checks reserves against possible payouts. The current interface supports buying and settlement, not selling shares back before the result.

A participant's account cannot bet on its own match. The market must be funded, opened and unpaused, and the match must be in play. In rooms, bets are accepted only during the 40-block window opened after a published Chaos point. No bet can enter a rally retroactively. The V4 market retains its collision guard. Quotes bind the game state; an outdated version can be rejected. These restrictions reduce latency advantages, but do not guarantee their elimination or identify every related wallet.

Chaos counts accepted MON costs toward crowd pressure. Beyond the threshold, stronger support shrinks the favourite's paddle at the next rally. Read the warning before signing. See Chaos rules and automatic payouts and refunds. All current betting is on Monad Testnet.

Winning bets, tournament prizes and refunds go to your wallet automatically. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate.

New Chaos markets use the first terminal Interlude result published on Monad, without waiting for delegation closure or the challenge period. This is an explicit testnet policy: a later successful challenge can change the result after the wallet has already received test MON. It is not irreversible protocol finality or a promise of instant delivery. The adapter reads the actual published participants, winner and result hash. Neither the VPS nor a caller supplies a winner. The first accepted result is fixed for that market; later disputes and corrections are recorded in a persistent operator audit, without reversing completed payments or paying a corrected winner again. A challenge already open at acceptance delays settlement until it is resolved. Receiving a payment needs neither a passkey ceremony nor an online recipient. Ordinary matches award ELO only, never a new MON prize. Game delegation renewal remains a separate lifecycle and can still pause new games; early payouts do not remove that limitation. Open your account, Betting credit & wallet, then Your recent positions. States include Position open, Waiting for result publication, Payment pending, Paid to your wallet, Payment delayed and Losing position � No payout. Payment transaction opens the receipt. Retry payment retries only a reserved debt to its fixed beneficiary. The worker attempts up to six automatic transfers before leaving further retries to the account. Funding and RPC outages can delay discovery or submission.

Existing markets remain bound to their original immutable adapter and vault. They still wait for delegation closure and the protocol challenge period. Choose Betting account to inspect current or previous betting credit and withdraw with a passkey. No balances or pending transactions are transferred to the new contracts. Each match keeps its original market.

In V4, winning bets, tournament prizes and eligible cancellation refunds are paid directly to the fixed beneficiary's Mera wallet. You do not need to click Claim, approve another passkey request or remain connected to receive them. A contract does not wake up by itself. The relayer discovers confirmed outcomes through Envio, verifies them against the contracts and submits the payment transactions. The contract fixes the recipient and amount; the caller cannot redirect the payment.

Open Wallet payments in the account panel to see the amount, origin, state and transaction link. Your wallet balance is shown separately from available betting credit. State What to do Payment pending Wait for discovery, transaction submission and confirmation Paid to your wallet Inspect the receipt and wallet balance; no claim is needed Payment delayed Read the error and use Retry payment when offered No payout for this bet The position lost or has no amount due; this is not a blocked claim

A rejected transfer leaves a reserved debt. Retries use that same beneficiary and debt, so they cannot pay twice. The relayer retries progressively, and a delayed receiver does not prevent another beneficiary's payment or the game's result. A confirmed cancelled match refunds accepted purchase costs under the market's rules. A confirmed cancelled tournament refunds entry fees; the seeded contribution is accounted for separately. A loss is not a cancellation and does not refund the losing bet. Funding, RPC or indexer outages can delay delivery. The payment history is the place to check the current result, not an assumed fixed delivery time.

Ordinary match wins award ELO when ranked, not MON prizes. V1–V3 claims still credit their old vaults and need a signed withdrawal. V4 wallet winnings are not automatically transferred into betting credit. Balance guide.
Recover from connection, input, audio and payment problems.

Use pongit.xyz over HTTPS and a PRF-capable passkey provider. Continue as… recovers the remembered account; Use another passkey selects a different credential. Creating another passkey creates another identity, not a repair of the old one. If the arcade session expired, click Reconnect in the header or Play now to renew directly. Close duplicate controlling tabs if the page reports another tab owns the session. Session guide.

Check Network details. Server round-trip, queue/preparation, broadcast, confirmation and snapshot age measure different parts of the path. A responsive local paddle does not mean the command is already included onchain. SYNCING / PREVIEW PAUSED means prediction reached its bound. Wait for a fresh snapshot. Do not hold another movement key to compensate for a disconnected transport. On reconnect, the contract state remains authoritative. Latency explanation.

section: A search or invitation seems stuck
text: Read the waiting screen and inbox. A pending invitation can expire or be declined; a submitted match transaction cannot be falsely cancelled. Check whether either opponent already has a match or queue. Avoid repeated invitations while an existing one is being created.

Open Arcade settings → Test sound. Check mute, both volume sliders, browser activation, tab mute and the physical output device. If the music load failed, retry through a user gesture after the connection recovers. Audio guide.

section: A bet failed or payment is delayed
text: Refresh the quote if it expired or the market locked. Check available betting credit and approve with the owner passkey. A failed quote does not imply a lost wallet transfer. For a due payment, inspect its history and receipt. Use Retry payment only when offered. A losing position correctly shows no payout. Older versions require their separate claim and withdrawal flow.

section: A replay or note is missing
text: A retired replay is intentionally no longer retained; its result and payments survive. Notebook edits need Save encrypted. A revision conflict requires reviewing the saved copy before discarding local work. When reporting an issue, include the browser, time, versioned match reference, visible error and public transaction hash. Never include a passkey secret, wallet key, session key or decrypted private notebook.
Quick answers and the language used around the arcade.
Gameplay gas is sponsored while the relayer is funded. Bets and fee-bearing tournament entries use test credits. Disabling a daily sponsorship ceiling does not make funding unlimited.

section: Do I get MON for every win?
text: No. Ordinary ranked games award ELO; friendly games award neither ELO changes nor a new MON prize. Winning bets and tournament prizes have their own accounting.

section: Do I need a wallet extension?
text: No. PONGIT uses a Mera passkey account. The provider must support PRF. Your public username is not your wallet or recovery credential.

section: Can I bet on myself or sell a position?
text: Participant accounts cannot bet on their own match. The current LMSR interface supports buying and settlement, not early resale.

section: Why are old claim buttons different?
text: V4 pays due amounts directly to the wallet. V1–V3 credit their old vaults and still require a signed withdrawal. Balances.

The Interlude lab is a separate Classic friendly arena with Mera sessions and spectators. The main arcade still uses Monad directly for its ranked games, Chaos, tournaments and financial operations. Engine response time and Monad commitment are different measurements.
The app retains the latest three eligible finished games per participant. Events remain onchain, but the site does not automatically rebuild retired replays.

Term Meaning in PONGIT MON The chain's native asset; this application currently uses test MON Gas Transaction execution cost, paid by the sponsor for supported gameplay Passkey / PRF Credential and deterministic key material used by Mera Arcade session A limited, expiring gameplay authorization ELO A rating based on ranked results and expected win probability Rally Play between two points; Chaos sizes stay fixed for that rally Vault Contract holding available betting credit Share A position paying proportionally if its side wins LMSR The binary market's cost function Relayer Service submitting supported signed actions and maintenance transactions Envio Indexer turning confirmed contract events into queryable records Snapshot An observed game state used for display and reconstruction Versioned reference Deployment plus match ID, such as v4:12 Settled result A confirmed authoritative outcome, not just a rendered preview

How the browser, relayer, Envio and Monad work together. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate.

PONGIT is a Next.js web application with Solidity contracts, a Node relayer and an Envio indexer. Production runs on a VPS behind Caddy HTTPS. PostgreSQL and internal services are private; the browser does not connect directly to the database. The rooms path is browser → hosted Solidity engine → published Monad state. The financial path is browser owner signature → persistent relayer → Monad market/vault. These paths have different confirmation guarantees. The following diagram describes the preserved V4 arcade:

Component Role Browser Passkey interaction, local input intent, bounded prediction, rendering and audio Game contract Match consent, block clock, collision physics, points, results and ratings Relayer Validate signed requests, persist jobs, submit transactions and track receipts Envio Index all supported deployments for history, replay retention, rankings and payment discovery Vault and markets Owner-approved spend, funded market accounting, settlement and native payouts Tournament contract Registration, seeding, round attachments, results, prizes and refunds

Mera derives the wallet from PRF-capable passkeys. An independent namespace powers the private notebook. The derived keys have different purposes; an arcade authorization never gains wallet spending rights. Envio provides indexed records rather than replacing the contracts' authority. Payment candidates are checked onchain before submission. Removing a retained replay does not remove settlement records.

The live transport is Monad Testnet, chain 10143, using public RPC services through application gateways. The site does not currently route transactions through Alchemy, and does not represent a sponsor integration as active just because it was considered. The main rooms arcade uses a multi-match Interlude engine. Mera signs a scoped SDK grant and game calls go directly to the hosted operator. Classic and Chaos results and ratings are computed in the Solidity application and published to Monad. The original single-arena lab and V4 are separate deployments. Chaos uses a testnet VPS attester to sign actual paid MON pressure at an exact between-rally cutoff. Its authority covers handicap input, not financial settlement. The new testnet settlement adapter captures the first published terminal result while its session is not challenged. It deliberately accepts correction risk; previous adapters still require hub status None after closure and the challenge period. The rooms coordinator indexes its own market events and reconciles contracts; it does not claim the new rooms stream is already an Envio replay pipeline. Envio continues to index V1 to V4. Scheduled renewal drains games, closes the delegation, waits the one-hour challenge period, finalizes results and verifies the hosted node's new epoch. This creates a game maintenance interval. New early testnet market payments do not wait for this lifecycle; previous market payments still do. No browser prediction or VPS signature can choose their winner.

The browser may display a prediction that differs from later confirmation. The relayer can delay or fail to submit, and Envio can lag. Immutable contracts constrain accepted actions, but the service does not claim censorship-proof scheduling or an independent security audit. Authentication boundaries.
The contract determines collisions; the browser makes the motion readable.

This section first describes the archived V4 arena. Current rooms use the engine transport described below; both keep contract state authoritative. The V4 deployment reuses GameV3 and PhysicsV2. Solidity and TypeScript share an event-driven model: positions and velocities have a 1,000,000 scale, time is in integer microseconds, division truncates toward zero and event times round up. The logical court is 1024 × 576, ball radius is 6, default paddle half-height is 48 and paddle speed is 180 logical units per second. The game ends at seven points. Chaos adds individual half-heights and a between-rally resume time.

Game time advances from active block numbers at 300,000 microseconds per block. The game accounts for paused blocks; this is a virtual clock, not a promise that every wall-clock block takes exactly 300 ms. Player or relayer timestamps cannot rewrite past collisions. An input takes effect at inclusion, after due events are resolved. Catch-up is bounded and resumable; Chaos stops at an intermission before resuming with fresh handicap values.

The client sends a signed intent without waiting for the previous receipt. The relayer retains one submitted, unconfirmed input per player plus the latest eligible pending intention. Intermediate unsent intentions can be superseded; signed transaction bytes are immutable. The existing onchain Input nonce remains strictly sequential. A dependent command waits for its predecessor on the server. After failure or expiry, the client refreshes state and re-signs the latest intention rather than creating a nonce gap.

The renderer reconstructs from a confirmed snapshot and relevant local intents, using a monotone browser clock. Prediction is bounded and corrections are smoothed. It stops extrapolating old snapshots indefinitely; SYNCING / PREVIEW PAUSED reports that limit. Contract collisions and scores remain authoritative.

Network details separates server round-trip, relayer queue/preparation, broadcast, chain/receipt observation, snapshot age and visual correction. Those measurements are not interchangeable. Client and server clocks must not be subtracted without synchronization. Moving the web frontend alone does not remove relayer queuing or Monad inclusion delay. Historical benchmarks are workload-specific, not present-day service guarantees. The source and test records include 10,000 differential physics cases per mode; those checks are correctness evidence, not a latency guarantee.

section: Current rooms: pushed state and recovery
text: Rooms can receive the contract's Snapshot events over one applied-event WebSocket per tab. Successful SDK receipts update the same cache. The initial getter supplies participants, nonces and clock metadata; events do not invent missing fields. A gap, restart, changed delegation or missing terminal winner requires an authoritative read. A consistency check runs every ten seconds while events remain fresh. If the stream is unavailable, reads are serialized with a 500 ms active-game interval and a two-second waiting interval. Remote Retry-After takes precedence. A failed write is reconciled with its receipt, state and SDK nonce before another command can be signed. A missing reply does not prove failure. Player A drives idle ticks at most every 300 ms. Player B takes over after 900 ms without progression; the VPS is the last fallback after 1.5 seconds. Successful inputs already advance the game and suppress unnecessary ticks. The server's maintenance scheduler can make its fallback later than the threshold. The browser still bounds preview when state is stale. A stream reduces repeated reads and stale-state corrections; it does not turn a live engine result into an irreversible Monad settlement or guarantee a particular network latency.

Public addresses and versioned references for V4 and its archives. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate.

The homepage uses the immutable multi-room application on Monad Testnet 10143, with separate Classic and Chaos ratings. The current rooms financial bindings are listed in the public manifest table below. New markets use a separate early testnet settlement adapter; original markets and their immutable financial bindings remain in deployments/rooms-finance.json.

V4 remains available separately. V4 deploys new immutable GameV3, ArcadeSessions and Vault instances with MarketV4 and TournamentsV4. The implementation name GameV3 is not the same as the application's deployment generation. The following tables are generated from the repository's public active manifest and its legacy chain. They expose only version, chain, start block and contract addresses. Follow each address to the testnet explorer.

Game, market, vault and tournament links are sealed before use. These contracts have no upgradeable proxy. A new deployment may inherit ratings, but existing balances and financial rights remain attached to the old contracts. The treasury is immutable where specified by the contract constructor. Replacing it requires a compatible new deployment, not an undocumented administrative edit to an existing match.

A rooms reference includes base chain, application address and full match identifier. A bare number or previous rooms URL must never silently resolve to another deployment. v4:12 means match 12 in V4. It is different from v3:12. Envio and private replay notes use deployment-qualified references. Active numeric API routes are scoped by /api/config; legacy reads require the chosen deployment parameter. Code must preserve the deployment when storing a receipt, replay, position or payout origin. Never assume a number alone identifies a match across upgrades.

V4 transfers due winnings and refunds to the fixed wallet recipient. V1–V3 claims credit their original vaults and need a signed withdrawal. A UI rollback must retain support for every deployment already accepted by the relayer journal. The source manifest includes deployment evidence. The permission model and operations guide explain the boundaries around these contracts.
Separate gameplay authorization, app access and owner-approved spending.

Authorization What it permits What it does not permit Owner passkey Wallet-approved spend, withdrawal, registration and authorized administration Bypassing contract roles or limits Arcade grant Own match consent, control, restoration and concession Betting, withdrawing or acting for another player App session Own profile, invitations, blocks and encrypted notebook access An arbitrary blockchain transfer

The EIP-712 arcade grant is bound to the player, game key, chain, registry, game contract, expiry and revocation state. Both owner and game-key signatures prove the delegation and possession. The maximum session duration is two hours. Match joins bind the opponent, room, commitment, session, nonce, expiry, tournament, mode, ranking choice and rules version. The existing Input signature binds its match, player, direction, sequential nonce and block-validity window. A revoked or expired key fails validation; replaying a nonce does not create another valid command. Only the limited arcade material and recovery data are stored in sessionStorage. The remembered passkey hint in localStorage is not the wallet key. Owner-derived keys are opened for their operation and closed afterward.

The server issues a single-use nonce and message bound to player, chain and game. A valid owner or active arcade signer exchanges the signed message for an HttpOnly, SameSite Strict cookie, Secure on production HTTPS. The current cookie lifetime is two hours; a session signed by an arcade key also depends on that key remaining valid. Private app routes check the cookie and the matching x-pongit-player header. State-changing app requests check the allowed Origin. This prevents a changed account in another tab from silently editing the previous account's profile.

A separate PRF namespace, pongit.xyz/notebook/v1, feeds HKDF and a nonextractable AES-GCM key. Each save uses a fresh 96-bit IV, account-bound authenticated data and revision-based concurrency control. Keys and plaintext stay in memory; stored ciphertext is not a guarantee against a compromised live browser.

Fixed-recipient payouts are permissionless to trigger or retry. No beneficiary signature is required because the caller cannot choose another recipient or change the debt. Spending permissions are unchanged. API reference.

Read application data and understand the authenticated transaction interfaces. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate.

HTTP base: https://pongit.xyz/api. WebSocket: wss://pongit.xyz/ws. This reference describes the delivered application interfaces, not an unrestricted RPC service. Examples are inert text: this documentation never executes a transaction. Large integer values are encoded as decimal strings; use bigint rather than JavaScript Number for wei, nonces and physics values. Mode 0 is Classic, 1 is Chaos. const response = await fetch('https://pongit.xyz/api/config'); if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Configuration unavailable'); const config = await response.json(); console.log(config.version, config.chainId, config.game);

Method and path Purpose / response GET /health ok , chain head, queue/funding error and payment worker status; 503 if unhealthy GET /config Active deployment, recursive legacy manifests, relayer and observed server time GET /matches Current match list in matches GET /matches/:id Match, clock, chain head and snapshot observation time; fresh=1 requests a fresh read GET /player/:address Ratings, balances, active game and authorization/nonces needed by the app GET /arcade/:address Current arcade authorization information GET /leaderboard?mode=0 Player rows with current ratings and public profile data GET /profiles?search=neon Up to 30 public prefix matches; also accepts a full address GET /profiles/:address Saved profile or the account's default avatar GET /player/:address/recent-matches Up to three cross-deployment summaries in Match GET /history?before=BLOCK Active deployment's result history, up to 100 rows GET /replay/:id?after=VERSION Up to 1000 Frame records after the version cursor GET /replay-status/v4:12 Replay availability for a qualified reference GET /tournaments Recent tournament data in tournaments GET /positions/:id/:address Paid cost, due amount, position state and payment details GET /payouts/:address?offset=0 Paginated account payment history GET /jobs/:id Sanitized transaction job state, receipt hash, error and timing GET /inputs/:id/:address Latest input-lane state for a match/player GET /alerts Indexed integrity signals, not automatic sanctions

POST /quote accepts matchId as a decimal string, side 0 or 1, and shares in base units. It returns amount, open, version, book and remainingUs. A quote is not a reservation or a transaction. {"matchId":"12","side":0,"shares":"1000000000000000"} POST /payouts/retry accepts an existing payment task id. It cannot specify a replacement recipient or amount. Throttling and onchain debt checks still apply.

POST /auth/challenge with player returns nonce, expires and the exact message to sign. POST /auth/session with player, nonce and signature establishes the app cookie. GET /auth/session checks it; DELETE /auth/session closes it. Do not invent or reuse the challenge message. Private app calls use browser credentials, an allowed Origin and x-pongit-player matching the authenticated account. Cookie possession does not authorize an onchain spend. Method and path Body / purpose PUT /profiles handle , avatar integer 0–11; returns the saved public profile DELETE /profiles Removes the authenticated public profile GET /notebook revision , and saved iv / ciphertext if present PUT /notebook Expected revision , base64url iv and ciphertext ; returns new revision GET /blocks Own blocked addresses POST or DELETE /blocks player address to block or unblock GET /challenges Own recent inbox, with expiry and room/transaction state POST /challenges recipient address or null for an open link, mode , ranked POST /challenges/rematch matchRef , such as v4:12 ; server verifies participation and derives opponent/rules GET /challenges/:id A visible invitation; addressed links enforce their recipient POST /challenges/:id/accept Accept and reserve the room atomically POST /challenges/:id/decline Decline a pending invitation POST /challenges/:id/cancel Cancel if eligible; a submitted job returns its actual state

POST /queue accepts a signed player request including player, expires, signature, tournamentId and mode. GET /queue/:address retrieves that player's queue/room state. POST /queue/cancel uses a signed cancellation. POST /ready supplies the room ticket and bilateral match consent. POST /inputs accepts { request, intent } and returns 202 after input-lane acceptance. request must target game.submitInput; the intent includes a signed client sequence. Lane states include accepted, superseded, submitted, confirmed and failed. Acceptance is not chain confirmation. POST /relay accepts deployment, contract, functionName and ABI-ordered args, returning a 202 job acknowledgement. Supported calls are allowlisted and simulated; arbitrary contract calls are not accepted. Journal jobs use queued, signed, sent, succeeded, failed and superseded. In particular, a confirmed successful receipt is exposed as succeeded, while the input lane calls that state confirmed. GET /jobs/:id returns tx_hash and timing with queueMs, broadcastMs, confirmationMs and totalMs; durations not yet observed are null. Owner signatures are required by financial contracts for purchases, withdrawals and registration. POST /faucet also verifies its signed test-credit request. Consult the actual typed-data and ABI definitions and client signing flow; the cookie is not a substitute. POST /rpc exposes selected JSON-RPC methods. Contract reads/estimates are restricted to known deployments; raw transaction submission is reserved for onchain administrators, with target and chain checks.

GET /legacy/player/:address, /legacy/claims/:address, /legacy/history, /legacy/matches/:id and /legacy/replay/:id select an archive using ?deployment=v1, v2 or v3. Without that parameter, the handler defaults to V1. Replay/history cursors retain their meanings. Legacy signed withdrawals go through the supported relay with the correct deployment. Never sign using the active V4 domain for a V1 vault.

The socket enforces the allowed Origin. It sends an initial head, then public head, match and job updates. Treat it as a notification feed and re-read current state after reconnecting; it is not a durable replay log. An authenticated app client may send: {"type":"subscribe-social","player":"0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001"} The player must match the app cookie. inbox is sent only to the relevant subscribed account; reload its inbox through HTTP. social-expired means authentication or account binding is no longer valid. The illustrated address is a placeholder, not a credential.

Read the returned error and HTTP status rather than assuming every failure is 401. The current server commonly returns 400 for validation/authentication failures, 404 for missing routes/jobs, 409 for notebook revision conflicts, 410 for retired replays, 429 for traffic limits and 503 for unhealthy service status. RPC errors follow JSON-RPC envelopes. Refresh expiring quotes and nonces after failure. Do not resend a different transaction for a job already signed or sent; recover its state and receipt first. No API route in this reference grants access to another player's private notebook.

POST /interlude/offers/accept with {id, operation} checks a duel before the SDK call. This HTTP response does not confirm engine consent. After a successful acceptMatch receipt, send {id, receiptHash, operation} to the same endpoint. The coordinator verifies the receipt's application, player and duel event before marking acceptance. alreadyAccepted: true means the client must observe the existing duel instead of sending another acceptance. The browser keeps a pending receipt hash in this tab's session storage so F5 can resume acknowledgement without another transaction. A failed or uncertain engine send stops automatic submission and offers Retry acceptance, which restores the SDK nonce and checks the duel first. An unstarted expired offer requires an explicit rejoin; it does not generate replacement tickets indefinitely. Upstream HTTP 429 responses retain Retry-After through the rooms API.

GET /interlude/config includes stateTransport (events or polling). The event adapter subscribes to interlude_subscribe("applied") on the deployment's node. It filters the application and subscription id, decodes contract events and reconciles discontinuities through the existing snapshot getter. The SDK still signs every command directly to the engine. An authenticated POST /interlude/presence heartbeat runs every ten seconds. rooms-changed notifications carry an account-specific revision and are sent only when the visible lobby changes. The browser coalesces refreshes and retains fallback polling. rooms-unavailable means the authorization service could not be reached: retain the local key, but do not perform unverified actions. rooms-expired is reserved for a verified invalid, revoked or expired session. Rooms errors retain error and add code, source, optional retryAt (Unix milliseconds) and requestId. ENGINE_RATE_LIMIT identifies an upstream 429; ENGINE_COOLDOWN identifies an action prevented locally during backoff. ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMIT and API_RATE_LIMIT identify PONGIT's separate budgets. SESSION_UNAVAILABLE returns 503; SESSION_REJECTED returns 401. ENGINE_PUBLICATION_UNAVAILABLE is a separate 503: the node has stopped accepting transactions because it cannot publish them. Recreating a player passkey does not repair publication. The relayer retains the exact pending transaction and slows its recovery checks; it does not replace that transaction or reset the sender nonce. POST /interlude/diagnostics accepts an ephemeral browser instance UUID and up to 200 payload-free samples. These private operational counters have no public read endpoint and expire after seven days. They exclude command parameters, signatures, private keys, cookies and notebook content.

These paths are under /api, use the rooms HttpOnly cookie, allowed Origin and matching x-pongit-player. /interlude/auth/challenge and /interlude/auth/session authenticate possession of the scoped SDK session key and verify the owner grant, app, chain, epoch and expiry. This is not a spending authorization. The private socket subscription is subscribe-rooms; after rooms-changed, reload HTTP state. A rooms-expired notification requires reconnection. Method and path Purpose GET /interlude/config App, rules, capacity, runtime admission and maintenance stage GET /interlude/finance Own rooms credit, wallet balance, vault/market nonces and recent positions GET /interlude/markets/:id?side=0&shares=1000000000000000 Quote, window version/cutoff, result, own position, payout and receipt POST /interlude/finance/credit Owner-signed expires and signature for this app's one-time test credit POST /interlude/finance/buy {bet, signature} using Bet typed data, the rooms market domain and fresh market nonce POST /interlude/finance/withdraw player , recipient , amount , nonce , deadline , owner signature bound to the rooms vault POST /interlude/finance/retry Match id ; the server derives this account's fixed payout identifier Financial mutations return the existing relayer job acknowledgement. GET /jobs/:id supplies the actual status and transaction hash. There is no public arbitrary rooms payload escape through /relay. All amounts and match ids are decimal strings; typed signatures bind chain 10143, exact contract and fresh sequential nonce. A quote is not a reservation. The game grant never signs a financial spend.

Authenticated GET /interlude/finance returns the current financial manifest, balances, nonces, history and archives for previous generations. Use ?financeId= for the original room account or ?financeId=early-v1 for the early testnet account. Responses from GET /interlude/markets/:id include the match's fixed financial manifest and settlementPolicy. Financial POST requests for buy, withdraw and credit include financeId for the intended account. A match cannot be reassigned to another market. EIP-712 spending signatures still target the selected market or vault address. A mismatched generation is rejected before enqueueing. Internal relayer jobs preserve roomApp and optional roomFinance; historical jobs without roomFinance keep their original destinations.

Operate the testnet service while preserving results and financial rights. Classic and Chaos rooms are open for testing. The hosted RPC may rate-limit requests and pause gameplay. This deployment is still undergoing multiplayer, payout and renewal validation. V4 balances and financial features remain separate.

Use More → Admin when the connected account has the onchain admin role, or open the administrator route. Merely viewing that route does not grant permission. Administration uses the owner passkey and a funded administrator account; it is not an arcade-key permission. The UI provides tournament creation, independent game/market pause and resume controls, and indexed integrity signals. Tournament creation requires its contract role and validates closing time, capacity, entry fee and funded prize. Signals are diagnostic and do not apply automatic sanctions.

Production runs the web app, relayer, Envio, Hasura, PostgreSQL, Caddy and separate RPC gateways on the VPS. Caddy manages HTTPS. Internal services and database credentials are not public browser endpoints. Gameplay commands take priority over payment and historical work. Sponsorship's daily ceiling is disabled, while balance reservations, gas-price limits, abuse quotas and market solvency constraints remain enforced. Monitor relayer funding and /api/health alongside queue, receipt and payment-worker errors.

Before a compatible release, record the active commit and images, create a private database/configuration backup and wait for active games to finish before restarting their services. Backups use seven-day retention with a protected offsite copy; that copy depends on the destination workstation being available. Service tests belong to a private, disposable VPS environment with separate chain, accounts, database and network. Never attach that environment to production financial state. Preserve the unique relayer nonce journal across application versions.

Recover already signed transactions from their persisted exact bytes and receipts. Do not delete the journal or reset the sender nonce to make a stuck queue disappear. Likewise, reconcile a restored database with the chain before allowing new writes. Use the repository's compatible V4 rollback procedure with an existing release. It verifies immutable contract bindings; an older V3-only binary is not a valid rollback after accepting V4 transactions. Application rollback does not reverse blockchain transactions. The operations runbook contains the maintained commands. Secrets, backup contents and operator credentials are intentionally excluded from this public guide.

Contracts are immutable and sealed. Replacing an immutable treasury requires redeployment. Financial debts reserved for rejected recipients cannot be reclaimed as treasury surplus. Keep all supported legacy withdrawals, claims and result references available during an upgrade. The isolated Interlude lab uses its own deployment manifest and operator-hosted node. Do not route V4 jobs or financial settlement through that node. Its delegation lifetime and any operator restart need separate monitoring and validation.

The rooms pressure and lifecycle keys are distinct from the financial relayer sender. Load their private read-only files through ROOMS_PRESSURE_KEY_FILE and ROOMS_LIFECYCLE_KEY_FILE; never put them in a manifest or client bundle. Enabling Chaos requires a sealed finance configuration and an enabled lifecycle worker. il_engine_jobs binds the engine sender nonce to app and delegation epoch. relay_jobs remains the unique financial journal and records exact finance app and round action. il_lifecycle_jobs records the operator's signed raw transactions before broadcast. Do not run another deployer command with that operator account while lifecycle processing owns its nonce. The lifecycle drains admission and active/publication work, closes the app, waits the hub's actual stakeUnlockAt, releases stake, freezes known final Chaos results and renews the same app. It admits players only after the node reports the renewed epoch. A challenge suspends automatic renewal. ROOMS_LIFECYCLE_HOLD_RENEW=true is a private operator hold after finalization for rehearsal or migration coordination. It does not shorten the challenge period. Keep rooms tables, accepted finance manifests and payment workers when rolling the UI back. Restoring a pre-rooms relayer binary would strand or misinterpret signed jobs. Do not delete pending transactions or reset nonces. Preserve V4 and earlier vault references, even after closing a rooms deployment. See the Chaos operations record.

ROOMS_STATE_STREAM_ENABLED=true enables the applied-event adapter on the server and advertises it to new browser sessions. Set it to false and restart the relayer to return to serialized polling while retaining the lobby, receipt and session-recovery fixes. This changes no contract or financial rule. An open tab can refresh after the flag changes. The additive il_presence, il_result_pending and il_rpc_diagnostics tables separate heartbeats, durable result processing and private measurements from the lobby document. Never drop the pending-result table during rollback: retained results must be reconciled before removing their jobs. Diagnostics aggregate counts per second, distinguish network calls from locally blocked attempts and retain data for seven days. They are not an independent source of scores, grants or payouts. Profile engine traffic by method and component, not just the total HTTP count. PONGIT's own account/IP guards are separate from an upstream quota. A 429 alone does not establish that quota. Include UTC times, method, response id and measured traffic windows when reporting an upstream rejection.

New testnet markets accept the first published Interlude result without the challenge wait. The relayer persists acceptance metadata, hub challenges, availability disputes, resolutions, unwinds and result-hash corrections in PostgreSQL. Inspect il_settlement_challenge_report and il_settlement_checks; join market payment receipts to verify actual transfers. Console events use rooms-settlement-audit and rooms-accepted-result-corrected. A challenge is not necessarily proven fraud. The audit records canonical and orphaned observations and does not issue compensation. Each market and queued transaction keeps its financial generation. Before renewing the game's delegation, the worker captures unsettled new-market results so a new epoch cannot strand them. Existing financial contracts and withdrawal rights remain available separately. See the repository's docs/EARLY_TESTNET_PAYMENTS.md for deployment and rollback procedures.
